html:
Nitaskinan is the homeland of the Atikamekw, an Algonquian people of the upper Saint-Maurice River in Quebec. Their name means "whitefish", and they call themselves Nehirowisiw.

They speak a language close to Cree. They lived by hunting, trapping, fishing and gathering, moving by canoe in summer and snowshoe in winter, and are known for birchbark baskets. They traded furs with New France from the 1600s. Logging, dams and railways cut into their land in the 1900s. Their three communities are Manawan, Wemotaci and Opitciwan.

In 2014 the Atikamekw declared their sovereignty over Nitaskinan. In 2020 the death of Joyce Echaquan, an Atikamekw woman, in a hospital at Joliette led to a national debate about racism in health care. Neighbours include the Innu and the Algonquin.
